ingredients.text: 1.5 cups Arborio rice (do not rinse, as starch is needed)
5 to 6 cups vegetable broth (kept warm in a separate pot)
1 lb mixed mushrooms (cremini, shiitake, oyster), sliced
2 tbsp vegan butter (or extra olive oil)
0.25 cup nutritional yeast (optional, for cheesy flavor)
Salt and black pepper to taste

instructions.title: Warm the Broth
instructions.text: Pour the vegetable broth into a saucepan and keep it on a low simmer next to your main cooking pot. Cold broth shocks the rice and stops the cooking process, preventing the creamy texture from developing.

instructions.title: Sauté the Mushrooms
instructions.text: In your heavy-bottomed pot, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until browned and their liquid has evaporated (about 5-8 minutes). Season with a pinch of salt. Remove mushrooms from the pot and set aside. This prevents them from getting rubbery during the rice cooking.

instructions.title: Aromatics and Toasting
instructions.text: Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil to the pot. Add shallots and cook until softened (2-3 minutes). Add garlic and thyme, cooking for another minute until fragrant. Add the Arborio rice. Toast the rice, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes until the edges are translucent and the center remains opaque. This toasting step creates a shell around the grain so it doesn't turn to mush while slowly releasing starch.

instructions.title: Deglaze
instructions.text: Pour in the white wine. Stir constantly until the wine is fully absorbed by the rice.

instructions.title: The Risotto Method
instructions.text: Begin adding the warm broth, one ladle (about 0.5 cup) at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until the liquid is almost completely absorbed before adding the next ladle. The friction from stirring rubs the grains together, releasing the starch that creates the creamy sauce. Repeat this process for about 20-25 minutes. The rice is done when it is tender but still has a slight bite (al dente).

instructions.title: The Finish (Mantecatura)
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. This is crucial. Stir in the cooked mushrooms, vegan butter, and nutritional yeast. Vigorously stir the mixture for 30 seconds to emulsify the fats with the starch. This step guarantees the creamy mouthfeel without dairy. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately.

phases.action: Chop vegetables, slice mushrooms, warm broth
Brown mushrooms, sweat shallots, toast rice
Add broth gradually, stir frequently to release starch
Remove from heat, beat in fat (mantecatura) for creaminess

props.text: This recipe creates a rich, velvety risotto for 4 people without using dairy. The key to the creamy texture lies in the high starch content of Arborio rice and the agitation process (stirring), which releases that starch into the broth.

This recipe assumes you have a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven. We assume the use of dry white wine, but you can substitute extra vegetable broth with a teaspoon of lemon juice or white wine vinegar for an alcohol-free version. Low-sodium vegetable broth is recommended.

The catch is that if any two players write the exact same clue, those clues are erased and the guesser never sees them. It forces players to be creative rather than obvious.

games.title: Deception: Murder in Hong Kong
games.description: One player is secretly the Murderer, and another is the Forensic Scientist who knows the solution but can only communicate by placing markers on scene tiles (like Cause of Death: Suffocation). The remaining players are investigators trying to interpret these vague clues to identify the murderer and the weapon used. It is less aggressive than other lying games because the focus is on the evidence.

games.title: The Resistance

Everyone votes to approve the team. If the mission goes ahead, players on the team secretly choose to Support or Sabotage the mission. The goal is to deduce who the saboteurs are based on voting patterns and mission results.

props.text: Visiting Kyoto in early April places you in the peak of spring season. While cherry blossoms (sakura) may be starting to flutter down by April 5-7, the city will be vibrant and busy. This itinerary balances the crowds by mixing popular historical sites with ample outdoor space for children. The schedule prioritizes locations with direct transit access or short taxi rides to strictly limit transit-to-destination walking to under 30 minutes.
To accommodate children ages 8 and 10 and the walking constraints, this plan utilizes a "hub" approach where you visit one major area in the morning and one in the afternoon.
**Transit Strategy:** Use JR lines and the subway where possible to avoid traffic. For Kiyomizu-dera, a taxi is recommended from the nearest station to save energy.
**Hiking Note:** The hikes selected (Monkey Park and Fushimi Inari) are the activities themselves, not transit walks. Both have rest stops and safe paths.
**Weather Framework:** Early April averages 10-20°C (50-68°F). Rain is possible, so indoor backups like the Railway Museum are included.
Families in Kyoto often prefer casual dining where noise levels are acceptable and menus are visual.
